reason: Re-opened al-Tabari on 51:56 to 51:57 (one segment) via packet.js quran 58 --verse 51.56. He sets out two readings (Zayd b. Aslam: the blessed created for worship, the wretched for disobedience; Ibn Abbas: to acknowledge servitude willingly or unwillingly), then in his own voice prefers Ibn Abbas’s, glossing it as created for Our worship and humbling to Our command, and answers the objection that they disbelieved: they have humbled themselves to His decree, which they cannot resist, and the disbeliever opposes Him only in acting on what He commanded. Evidence words found verbatim; the sentence states his preference only where he states it (trap satisfied) and the since-clause is his own answer. Plain sense checked against day.js: 51:54 to 51:55 tell the Prophet to withdraw and to warn, and 51:56 is the singular first person ‘I created’. verse.js ok (Adh-Dhariyat 51:56, at 4730); entry-check ok, no warns. Minor weaknesses that do not break it: ‘them’ has no antecedent in the sentence (it leans on the key verse printed above), and ‘humble themselves before His command’ followed by ‘defy only His commands’ reads as a paradox in English, though it is al-Tabari’s own amr/qadāʾ distinction and the sentence gives his resolution.
better: Optional clarity edit on the same evidence: ‘al-Tabari, on 51:56 to 51:57, takes jinn and humankind, with Ibn Abbas, as made to worship and bow to Him, since even deniers bow to His decree and defy only what He commands.’
